messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

message.content:
A good rule‑of‑thumb for a typical U.S. home is **about 5 kWh of electricity per square foot per year**.  
For a 2,000 sq ft house that works out to roughly:

| Metric | Estimate |
|--------|----------|
| Annual electricity use | **≈ 10 000 kWh** (range 9 000–12 000 kWh) |
| Daily average | **≈ 27–33 kWh/day** |
| Monthly average | **≈ 800–1 000 kWh/month** |

### Why the range?

| Factor | Effect on consumption |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Climate** | Hot climates (AC use) → higher; cold climates (heating) → higher |
| **Insulation & windows** | Poor insulation → more heating/cooling → higher |
| **Appliances & electronics** | Energy‑efficient appliances lower usage |
| **Occupancy & habits** | More occupants or longer hours of use raise consumption |
| **Renewable integration** | Solar or wind can offset part of the load |

If you’re planning a solar system, you can plug these numbers into a solar‑panel calculator to see how many panels you’d need. Let me know if you’d like help with that!
